name: SQL Injection
objective: Keep untrusted data separate from SQL syntax.
technology: ORMs with raw query escape hatches

applicability.when: The application constructs or executes SQL using externally influenced data.
applicability.not_applicable_when: There is no SQL query execution in the selected scope.

failure_patterns: Assuming ORM use makes raw SQL safe
detection: Trace request, job, and import inputs to query sinks; inspect stored procedures too.
Distinguish bound values from dynamic identifiers and inspect driver parameter APIs.
remediation: Bind data values using driver parameters.
Allowlist identifiers and sort directions; reduce database account privileges.
verification: Test an injection-shaped value against a local seeded database and show it is treated as data.
Assert ordinary queries still return only intended rows.
severity: Often High; increase with unauthenticated access, broad read/write privileges, or sensitive data. Syntax warnings alone do not establish impact.
automation_limits: Static matches need data-flow and driver semantics review; live database permissions and reachable routes may be unavailable.

name: Cross-Site Scripting
objective: Prevent untrusted input from becoming executable browser content.

applicability.when: Untrusted data reaches browser-rendered HTML, script, URL, or DOM contexts.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No browser-rendered content exists in scope.

failure_patterns: Trusting stored content or disabling template escaping
detection: Trace reflected, persisted, and client-side sources to rendering sinks.
Review sanitizer configuration and unsafe URL schemes in the correct context.
remediation: Use framework contextual escaping and safe DOM APIs.
Sanitize intentionally supported HTML with a maintained sanitizer; use CSP as defense in depth.
verification: Exercise reflected, stored, and DOM routes locally with harmless execution markers.
Check legitimate rich content and URL rendering are preserved.
severity: Usually Medium to High depending on victim privileges, reach, and accessible data; self-only execution may have lower impact.
automation_limits: Server-only scans miss client flows and browser behavior; CSP presence alone does not prove XSS prevention.

name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
objective: Ensure state-changing requests reflect the authenticated user's intent.

applicability.when: A browser automatically attaches credentials to state-changing requests, including session cookies or HTTP authentication.
applicability.not_applicable_when: Endpoints require non-ambient credentials and do not accept ambient-authenticated alternatives; document that evidence.

failure_patterns: Relying solely on CORS or loosely configured SameSite
detection: Inventory credential mechanisms per endpoint, including login and alternate form content types.
Review token binding, origin checks, and framework CSRF middleware coverage.
remediation: Use framework CSRF tokens or robust origin verification suited to the architecture.
Use appropriate SameSite cookies as additional protection; avoid state-changing safe methods.
verification: Show a legitimate action succeeds and missing/invalid anti-CSRF evidence is rejected.
Test cross-origin form requests and login CSRF where relevant.
severity: Medium to High when unwanted actions change accounts, privileges, or funds; assess prerequisites and browser cookie behavior.
automation_limits: CORS does not stop simple cross-origin requests. Bearer-only APIs generally differ from cookie sessions; deployment behavior needs browser validation.

name: File Upload Security
objective: Constrain uploaded content, processing cost, and access.

applicability.when: Users or integrations can submit files or archives for storage or processing.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No file ingestion exists in the selected scope.

failure_patterns: Executable public storage or path traversal
Unbounded decompression or processor resource use
detection: Inspect upload handlers, storage names, serving headers, and processor invocation.
Review allowed formats, size/count limits, malware strategy, and authorization.
remediation: Allowlist required formats and validate content with suitable parsers; MIME headers are untrusted.
Generate storage identifiers, isolate storage from execution, enforce quotas, and sandbox processors.
verification: Use benign mismatched formats, traversal names, and bounded oversized inputs.
Verify downloads enforce authorization and valid files still work.
severity: High for code execution or cross-user data exposure; resource exhaustion and unsafe active content vary with deployment.
automation_limits: A parser or antivirus result cannot prove a file harmless; processor versions, serving behavior, and storage policy require review.

name: Broken Object-Level Authorization
objective: Enforce ownership and tenant boundaries for every object operation.

applicability.when: Callers access objects identified by IDs, paths, or other selectors.
applicability.not_applicable_when: There are no caller-dependent object access rules in scope.

failure_patterns: Lookup by ID without caller scope
Authorization on UI lists but not direct or batch endpoints
detection: Trace read/write/delete/export paths from identity to object selection.
Build a subject-object-action matrix for owners, other users, tenants, and administrators.
remediation: Scope lookups to authorized subjects/tenants and enforce policy server-side.
Cover nested, batch, and asynchronous operations; opaque IDs supplement authorization.
verification: Assert owner access succeeds and another user/tenant is denied without data leakage.
Test every applicable action and role, including legitimate administrator behavior.
severity: High for sensitive cross-user or tenant access; impact depends on accessible data and write powers, not ID guessability alone.
automation_limits: Scanners rarely know ownership policy. Manual policy definition and at least two identities are normally required.

name: Rate Limiting
objective: Bound abuse and expensive resource consumption without blocking normal use.

applicability.when: Untrusted callers can repeatedly invoke authentication, costly operations, or scarce resources.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No repeatable untrusted entry point or constrained resource exists in scope.

detection: Identify abuse-sensitive actions and cost drivers; inspect gateway and application controls.
Check identity/IP/device dimensions, trusted proxy handling, quotas, and failure behavior.
remediation: Use layered limits and quotas by appropriate subjects, with bounded payloads, queues, and execution time.
Avoid account lockouts that enable denial of service; return usable retry information.
verification: Use a small bounded local burst to show enforcement and recovery.
Verify normal usage and multi-instance/shared-store assumptions without production load testing.
severity: Medium to High for account takeover facilitation, large costs, or outages; required thresholds depend on the service.
automation_limits: Source review cannot establish safe production capacity, distributed enforcement, or abuse thresholds; never stress a live service by default.

name: JWT Security
objective: Accept only authentic tokens intended for this issuer, audience, and use.

applicability.when: The application issues or consumes JWTs.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No JWTs are used; opaque sessions need separate review.

failure_patterns: Arbitrary key URLs or token-type confusion
detection: Review verification options, algorithm allowlists, key provenance, and claim validation.
Separate ID tokens from access tokens and review key rotation and caching.
remediation: Use maintained libraries with explicit algorithms and trusted keys.
Validate required issuer, audience, expiration, and token purpose; constrain clock skew and key selection.
verification: Reject tampered, expired, wrong-audience, wrong-issuer, and unexpected-algorithm tokens.
Accept a valid intended token and exercise key rotation locally.
severity: High if authentication or privilege claims can be forged; shorten severity claims when only speculative library usage is known.
automation_limits: Decoding is not verification. Library defaults differ; revocation and key lifecycle require operational evidence.

name: Secret and API Key Exposure
objective: Keep credentials out of public artifacts and minimize exposure.

applicability.when: The project uses credentials or may have included them in source or artifacts.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No credential-bearing feature/artifact exists, with bounded inventory evidence; unknown history remains unverified.

failure_patterns: Server secrets embedded in browser builds
Secrets in history, examples, or build output
detection: Review tracked files, ignored-config practices, generated public assets, and available local history.
Classify synthetic placeholders separately; never test a discovered credential against its provider.
tools: Gitleaks dir and git modes with redaction
Agent review of public bundle inputs
remediation: Revoke and rotate exposed credentials through the owner's approved process.
Move secrets to suitable runtime storage; history cleanup alone does not revoke a credential.
verification: Verify the current artifact no longer exposes the value and configuration loads correctly.
Obtain owner evidence of revocation and assess history/copies; mask evidence.
severity: High to Critical for usable privileged credentials; an obvious synthetic value is not evidence of a valid secret.
automation_limits: Patterns miss opaque secrets and can flag examples. Local history may be shallow; credential validity must not be probed without explicit authorization.

name: Password Storage
objective: Make stolen password databases expensive to attack and avoid credential disclosure.

applicability.when: The application stores or verifies user passwords.
applicability.not_applicable_when: Authentication is fully delegated and the application never handles passwords; review the identity provider boundary separately.

failure_patterns: Passwords in logs, exceptions, or reset messages
detection: Inspect hashing API, salt generation, work factors, pepper handling, and rehash-on-login logic.
Trace password handling through registration, reset, import, and error paths.
remediation: Use a maintained adaptive password hash, preferably Argon2id with parameters appropriate to resources.
Follow current framework/OWASP guidance for legacy bcrypt limits and migration; never implement custom cryptography.
verification: Check unique salts, supported cost parameters, successful/failed verification, and safe migration.
Confirm password values are absent from captured logs.
severity: High for plaintext/reversible storage; weak work factors depend on realistic offline attack cost and exposed data.
automation_limits: Parameter strength changes with hardware and policy; unit tests cannot demonstrate resistance to all offline attacks.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication
objective: Protect high-risk access and recovery with appropriately independent factors.

applicability.when: Risk, contract, or policy requires MFA, particularly for privileged or sensitive actions.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No MFA requirement is justified by the documented risk model; absence alone is not automatically a vulnerability.

failure_patterns: Reusable OTPs or unenforced administrator policy
detection: Review enforced IdP/application policy, enrollment, step-up, recovery, and factor reset.
Check phishing resistance, replay protection, attempt limits, and recovery notifications.
remediation: Prefer phishing-resistant factors where supported; enforce policy on every relevant route.
Secure reset/recovery to comparable assurance and provide a safe recovery procedure.
verification: Test required-role enforcement, one-time use, invalid attempts, and legitimate recovery.
Verify factor removal and enrollment require appropriate authentication.
severity: High for bypass of required privileged MFA; missing optional MFA needs a documented risk assessment before classification.
automation_limits: Source alone may not show IdP policy; account recovery and support processes need human review.

name: CORS Security
objective: Allow browser cross-origin reads only where the application's policy intends them.

applicability.when: The service returns CORS headers or supports cross-origin browser access.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No browser cross-origin access or CORS policy exists in scope.

detection: Review origin parsing, allowlists, credential use, and proxy-added headers.
Distinguish public unauthenticated APIs from responses containing private user data.
remediation: Use exact required origins including scheme and port, with narrow methods and headers.
Enable credentials only when required; emit Vary: Origin for dynamically selected origins.
verification: Test allowed and disallowed origins, null origin, preflight, and actual requests.
Verify authenticated private data cannot be read by an untrusted origin.
severity: Medium to High when private data is readable; wildcard origin on a public credential-free API may be intentional.
automation_limits: CORS is a browser read boundary, not authentication or CSRF prevention. Browsers reject wildcard Allow-Origin with credentialed reads; that pair alone is not proof of data theft.

name: Authentication Token Storage
objective: Limit authentication-token exposure to scripts, transport, and unrelated requests.

applicability.when: Clients or servers persist authentication tokens.
applicability.not_applicable_when: There are no persisted authentication tokens within the selected scope.

failure_patterns: Long-lived tokens in localStorage without an assessed tradeoff
Broad cookie domain or token exposure in URLs
detection: Inventory each token, lifetime, storage location, consumer, and trust boundary.
Review cookie scope, SameSite needs, mobile secure storage, and frontend XSS exposure.
tools: Browser storage/cookie inspection on a local test instance
remediation: Prefer protected cookies where suitable, with Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite/scope.
Account for CSRF when moving to cookies; use platform secure storage for native clients and minimize token lifetime.
verification: Assert relevant cookie flags and scope, and confirm scripts cannot read HttpOnly tokens.
Test legitimate login/cross-site flows; ensure URLs and logs contain no tokens.
severity: Medium to High depending on token privilege, lifetime, and attacker capabilities; storage choice alone does not demonstrate an exploit.
automation_limits: HttpOnly does not stop all actions through an XSS-compromised page. Browser and native storage models differ; design tradeoffs require review.

name: Server-Side Authorization
objective: Enforce role and operation permissions at trusted execution points.

applicability.when: Operations have role-, permission-, or policy-dependent access.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No privileged or identity-dependent operations exist in the selected scope.

failure_patterns: Unprotected alternate routes or HTTP methods
Trusting client-supplied roles or tenant claims
detection: Inventory privileged operations and map policy to middleware and service-layer checks.
Review default-deny behavior, mass assignment, job invocation, and alternate interfaces.
remediation: Enforce trusted server-side policy with deny-by-default behavior.
Centralize reusable policy decisions while checking each entry point and writable property.
verification: Test anonymous, ordinary, and privileged callers across routes and methods.
Verify forbidden fields are ignored/rejected and authorized workflows remain usable.
severity: High to Critical for privileged state changes; separate operation-level authorization from object ownership in SEC-05.
automation_limits: Route decorators alone do not prove complete policy enforcement; business roles and internal trust assumptions need owner input.

name: Database Row-Level Security
objective: Make existing database row policies enforce intended tenant and user isolation.

applicability.when: The architecture uses RLS, or explicitly relies on database row policies for isolation.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The architecture does not use or require RLS; assess application-level access using SEC-05 and SEC-13.

failure_patterns: Missing write policies or unsafe tenant context
detection: Inspect migrations and effective policies with the actual application database role.
Review owners, superusers, BYPASSRLS, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, pooling, and trusted identity context.
remediation: Constrain read and write policies to the intended identity/tenant model.
Avoid bypass-capable application roles; bind trusted per-request context safely, including pooled connections.
verification: Test cross-tenant reads, inserts, updates, and deletes using the real application role.
Verify connection reuse cannot retain another tenant's identity and legitimate operations succeed.
severity: High for cross-tenant access under a relied-on policy; missing RLS alone is not a finding.
automation_limits: Policy behavior is vendor-specific. Schema text cannot establish effective production role privileges or managed-service identity settings.

name: Webhook Verification
objective: Accept authentic, fresh events and process retries without duplicate effects.

applicability.when: External services deliver events that influence application state.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No inbound webhook/event-callback boundary exists.

detection: Review provider-specific verification over exact raw bytes before processing.
Trace secret lookup, timestamp tolerance, event IDs, retries, and transactional idempotency.
remediation: Use the provider's verification library and approved secret rotation.
Enforce suitable freshness/replay rules and atomic idempotency keyed to trusted event identity.
verification: Reject tampered bodies, invalid signatures, and stale events as appropriate to the protocol.
Replay and concurrently deliver a valid event; verify one effect and safe legitimate retry.
severity: High for payment/account manipulation; distinguish signature authenticity, replay detection, and business idempotency.
automation_limits: Not every provider signs timestamps; follow its protocol rather than inventing headers. Static checks cannot verify provider configuration.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery
objective: Prevent untrusted destinations from reaching unintended networks or credentials.

applicability.when: Untrusted input influences a server-side network destination.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No server-side fetching destination is externally influenced.

failure_patterns: DNS rebinding or access to metadata/private addresses
detection: Trace URLs through parsing, DNS resolution, redirects, proxies, and connection APIs.
Inspect egress restrictions, credential forwarding, and supported schemes/ports.
remediation: Prefer exact known destinations and narrow protocols/ports.
Enforce resolved-address and redirect policy at connection time; isolate egress and strip unintended credentials.
verification: Use local mocks for forbidden private/metadata destinations and redirect changes; never probe real metadata services.
Verify intended destinations work and rebinding/IPv6 normalization cases are addressed.
severity: High to Critical when internal services or cloud credentials become reachable; simple URL acceptance alone is insufficient.
automation_limits: Correct DNS/connection enforcement depends on the HTTP client and deployment network. Static analysis often cannot prove runtime destination safety.

name: Source Map Exposure
objective: Prevent public debugging artifacts from disclosing information outside the intended public bundle.

applicability.when: Production builds generate source maps or publish debugging artifacts.
applicability.not_applicable_when: There are no production source maps or browser bundles in scope.

failure_patterns: Publishing embedded private source or credentials
Assuming disabling sourceMappingURL removes deployed files
detection: Review build configuration and the actual local release artifact.
Determine whether map contents add sensitive information beyond already-public code and inspect upload destination controls.
remediation: Remove sensitive values from all client builds, regardless of source maps.
Restrict source maps to trusted error tracking or publish intentionally only after content review.
verification: Inspect generated release files and authorized deployment evidence for direct map access.
Verify debugging still works through the intended restricted channel.
severity: Informational to High according to actual disclosed content; source-map presence alone is not automatically a vulnerability.
automation_limits: Source maps can be intentionally public. Local build settings do not prove CDN contents or cache invalidation.

name: Default Credentials
objective: Prevent deployment with known passwords, bootstrap accounts, or unsafe development modes.

applicability.when: The application provisions accounts or includes development/bootstrap configuration.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No account provisioning or environment-sensitive development configuration exists in scope.

failure_patterns: Debug mode enabled in production profile
Fail-open fallback when required configuration is absent
detection: Review install/bootstrap paths, sample configuration, and environment defaults.
Inspect whether provisioning secrets must be changed and development services are exposed.
remediation: Require unique securely provisioned credentials and disable unnecessary defaults.
Make production configuration fail closed without echoing secrets; isolate development profiles.
verification: Show an unchanged default is refused or cannot access privileged resources.
Test missing required settings and legitimate secure production-profile startup locally.
severity: High to Critical for exposed privileged defaults; insecure-looking settings unused outside a local fixture need context.
automation_limits: Runtime provisioning and deployment overrides may be invisible; do not try default passwords against live systems without authorization.

name: Sensitive Information in Logs
objective: Keep credentials and unnecessary personal data out of logs and diagnostics.

applicability.when: The application emits operational logs, traces, or diagnostics.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No logging/diagnostic surface exists in the selected scope, with evidence.

failure_patterns: Tokens in URLs or exception objects
Sensitive tracing attributes sent to third parties
detection: Trace authentication and sensitive data through loggers, middleware, and exporters.
Review redaction before serialization, access, retention, and log injection handling.
remediation: Use structured allowlisted logging and redact at the earliest shared boundary.
Restrict log access/retention and avoid logging raw credentials or request bodies by default.
verification: Exercise success/error paths with synthetic markers and inspect captured outputs.
Verify useful request identifiers remain and multiline input cannot forge log records.
severity: High for usable credentials in accessible logs; personal-data impact depends on sensitivity, retention, and readership.
automation_limits: Redaction patterns cannot cover all secret or personal-data formats; external log storage and historical deletion require human evidence.

name: Vulnerable Dependencies
objective: Identify known vulnerable resolved components and assess realistic application exposure.

applicability.when: The application depends on third-party components, directly or transitively.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No third-party components are used in the selected scope; platform dependencies may remain outside scope.

detection: Inventory actual resolved versions, supported lockfiles, vendored code, and deployment runtime.
Review advisory conditions, reachability, compensating controls, and scan database freshness.
remediation: Upgrade to supported fixed versions and review migration impact.
Use a documented compensating control or time-bounded exception when no safe upgrade exists.
verification: Recheck resolved artifacts against the advisory and run affected legitimate behavior tests.
Record scanner/database version, exclusions, failures, and residual advisories.
severity: Use advisory severity as input, then assess installed version, exposure, and exploit prerequisites; tool ratings are not automatic application severity.
automation_limits: Offline databases age; scanners miss unknown flaws and unsupported ecosystems. No advisory does not prove safety; a version match need not establish exploitability.

name: Business Logic Vulnerabilities
objective: Enforce business invariants despite valid-looking but adversarial workflows.

applicability.when: The application enforces domain-specific rules or workflows.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No security-relevant business invariant exists in the selected component.

failure_patterns: Trusting client prices or discount eligibility
Negative quantities, replayed credits, or rounding abuse
detection: Ask the owner for invariants and forbidden outcomes; map trust in external inputs.
Review state machines, payment reconciliation, currency/quantity boundaries, and bypass routes.
remediation: Recompute authoritative values server-side and constrain state transitions.
Use explicit validation, transactional invariants, and trusted payment reconciliation.
verification: Test forbidden transitions, altered price/quantity, replay, and boundary cases.
Verify legitimate refunds, retries, approvals, and failure recovery still work.
severity: High to Critical for unauthorized transfers or entitlements; quantify business impact with the owner rather than inventing loss estimates.
automation_limits: Scanners cannot infer product rules. Missing business context is UNVERIFIED; passing happy-path tests is insufficient.

name: OAuth and OpenID Connect Security
objective: Bind authorization responses and identities to the intended client, request, and account.

applicability.when: The application implements OAuth/OIDC login, delegation, or account linking.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No OAuth or OpenID Connect integration exists.

failure_patterns: Account linking based on unverified email or unvalidated ID tokens
detection: Review exact registered redirects, code flow, PKCE S256, and CSRF/request binding.
For OIDC validate signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce where required; distinguish access and ID tokens.
remediation: Follow current OAuth security BCP and provider requirements using maintained libraries.
Prefer authorization code with PKCE; validate state or a protocol-appropriate CSRF binding and require authenticated intent for linking.
verification: Reject wrong state/binding, incorrect PKCE verifier, unexpected redirects, and invalid identity claims.
Exercise normal login, denial, logout implications, and explicit account linking.
severity: High to Critical for account takeover or token theft; judge protocol-specific defenses instead of requiring every mechanism in every flow.
automation_limits: Identity-provider registrations and redirect behavior need configuration evidence; state and nonce serve different purposes.

name: Session Management
objective: Bound session lifetime and invalidate sessions at relevant security events.

applicability.when: The application maintains authenticated state across requests.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No authenticated persistent state exists in scope.

failure_patterns: Logout only removes a UI token
Unlimited idle/absolute lifetime or unsafe refresh reuse
detection: Trace session creation, identifier rotation, expiry, logout, password changes, and privilege changes.
Review refresh token rotation/reuse detection and distributed invalidation.
remediation: Rotate identifiers after authentication/privilege changes and use suitable idle/absolute expiry.
Invalidate server-side sessions where supported; for stateless tokens document revocation strategy and residual lifetime.
verification: Test fixation attempts, expiry boundaries, logout reuse, and relevant security-event revocation.
Verify ordinary session renewal and concurrent device behavior follow policy.
severity: Medium to High according to session privilege and residual attacker access; stateless-token logout limitations need explicit risk treatment.
automation_limits: Source review does not prove distributed revocation or session-store behavior; client deletion does not invalidate stolen stateless tokens.

name: HTTP Security Headers
objective: Use browser security policies suited to the content and deployment.

applicability.when: The application serves browser content or HTTPS endpoints where relevant policies apply.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The reviewed component serves no applicable HTTP/browser response; evaluate each header separately.

failure_patterns: HSTS applied without verifying HTTPS subdomain readiness
detection: Review effective headers at application/proxy boundaries across success/error responses.
Assess CSP sources/nonces, frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, nosniff, referrer policy, and HSTS requirements.
remediation: Deploy an appropriate CSP and frame policy, testing integrations first.
Use HSTS only with operational HTTPS readiness; review includeSubDomains/preload impacts before enabling.
verification: Verify actual responses and error paths, browser CSP behavior, and permitted embeds.
Ensure restrictive policies do not break legitimate scripts or required framing.
severity: Often Low to Medium alone; increase only with demonstrated exploit context. HSTS and CSP relevance differs for non-browser APIs.
automation_limits: A generic header score is not an application assessment. CSP report-only is observation, and deprecated headers are not a substitute for current protections.

name: Transport and Data Encryption
objective: Protect sensitive data in transit and at rest with an appropriate key lifecycle.

applicability.when: Sensitive data crosses network boundaries or persists in storage.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No sensitive network transmission or storage exists in the selected scope.

failure_patterns: Encryption keys stored beside broadly readable ciphertext
detection: Map sensitive flows and storage including caches, backups, and service-to-service links.
Review TLS validation, current library defaults, key access, rotation, and recovery procedures.
remediation: Use supported TLS with certificate/hostname verification and maintained cryptographic libraries.
Use authenticated encryption/storage services where appropriate; separate key access and plan rotation/recovery.
verification: Reject invalid certificates with a local test endpoint; test intended trust chains.
Verify encrypted storage configuration and unauthorized key denial without printing plaintext or keys.
severity: High for interceptable sensitive data or broad key access; at-rest requirements depend on threat model and data classification.
automation_limits: Application code cannot prove cloud disk encryption, backup protection, or key custody. Encryption does not replace authorization.

name: Cloud and Infrastructure Permissions
objective: Limit infrastructure access and exposure to required subjects and resources.

applicability.when: The application has deployment infrastructure or cloud resources in scope.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The selected component has no deployment resources in its documented architecture. If a deployment exists but effective settings are unavailable, use UNVERIFIED.

failure_patterns: Wildcard IAM or overly privileged service accounts
Exposed management ports or privileged containers
detection: Review IaC, role trust policies, network boundaries, storage ACLs, and workload identities.
Compare intended permissions to available read-only effective-policy evidence and drift records.
remediation: Reduce permissions to required actions/resources and isolate public/private surfaces.
Prefer scoped workload identity over static credentials; stage policy changes with rollback access.
verification: Use local policy tests or authorized policy simulation to check allowed/denied actions.
Have operators confirm effective deployed state and legitimate workload behavior.
severity: High to Critical for sensitive public resources or administrative access; broad-looking policy syntax needs effective-context review.
automation_limits: IaC may differ from deployment, and effective IAM is compositional. Do not enumerate accounts or change infrastructure without explicit scope.

name: CI/CD Pipeline Security
objective: Prevent untrusted changes from gaining trusted build credentials or publication authority.

applicability.when: The project builds, tests, or releases through a CI/CD pipeline.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No pipeline/build-automation boundary exists in scope.

failure_patterns: Privileged jobs execute untrusted pull-request code
Shell interpolation of untrusted event data
Mutable action refs or persistent broad credentials
detection: Trace event triggers, permissions, checkout refs, third-party actions, caches, artifacts, and release gates.
Review whether build/install hooks run before trust is established and whether logs expose credentials.
remediation: Use minimal permissions, immutable reviewed action pins, and isolated untrusted jobs.
Pass untrusted values as data rather than shell code; gate publication and restrict reusable credentials.
verification: Inspect representative fork-PR and trusted-release execution paths without publishing.
Run local workflow checks and verify untrusted jobs cannot access release secrets.
severity: High to Critical when arbitrary changes reach secrets or releases; action pinning alone cannot make untrusted code safe.
automation_limits: Hosted settings, environment protection, and runner persistence need owner evidence; do not execute suspicious workflows to test them.

name: Race Conditions
objective: Preserve security and business invariants under concurrent operations.

applicability.when: Concurrent requests can alter a shared security-sensitive resource.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No shared mutable state or concurrency-sensitive invariant exists in scope.

failure_patterns: In-memory locks in a multi-process deployment
detection: Identify invariants, transaction boundaries, unique constraints, locks, and retry handling.
Review isolation level and external side effects under concurrent retries.
remediation: Use atomic updates, suitable transactions/locks, and database uniqueness constraints.
Couple idempotency to durable state and reconcile external effects; avoid process-only locks for distributed systems.
verification: Coordinate a small number of local workers against the same operation.
Assert at most one effect and expected losers/retries, then verify normal sequential use.
severity: High for double spending or privilege/ownership bypass; quantify whether duplicates violate an actual invariant.
automation_limits: Passing stress tests does not prove absence of races. Isolation semantics and real deployment topology require reasoning and integration evidence.

name: Backup and Recovery Security
objective: Make recovery data confidential, access-controlled, and demonstrably restorable.

applicability.when: The service stores durable state or has backup/recovery obligations.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The selected component is stateless with no recovery data or obligation; missing backup evidence for a stateful system is UNVERIFIED.

failure_patterns: Untested restores or retention that conflicts with policy
detection: Review backup access/encryption, retention, separation from compromised production identities, and documented RPO/RTO.
Inspect dated restore evidence and dependency/key recovery plans; never restore over production.
remediation: Protect backup data and keys with scoped access, monitored recovery procedures, and suitable isolation/immutability.
Define retention and perform documented restores in an isolated environment.
verification: Use synthetic data for a bounded restore drill and verify integrity and access denial.
Record measured recovery behavior against owner-defined objectives and remaining dependencies.
severity: High for sensitive backup disclosure or inability to recover critical data; RPO/RTO adequacy is an owner decision.
automation_limits: Repository files cannot prove backups exist or restore successfully. Restoration is potentially destructive and requires an explicitly approved isolated destination.

name: AI and Agent Security
objective: Constrain untrusted model inputs and actions at enforceable trust boundaries.

applicability.when: The application uses AI models, agent tools, retrieval, or model-driven actions.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The application has no AI or agent feature; using this toolkit to review it does not make SEC-30 applicable.

failure_patterns: Broad tool access or implicit approval
Secrets in prompts, traces, or model-triggered requests
detection: Map untrusted direct/retrieved inputs to model context, tool calls, memory, and output consumers.
Review per-user authorization at tool execution, sandbox boundaries, egress, sensitive data, and approval gates.
remediation: Enforce least privilege and authorization outside the model; require approval for consequential actions.
Treat model output as untrusted, minimize secrets, isolate tools, and constrain destinations and data access.
verification: Use benign direct/indirect injection text with mocked tools to attempt unauthorized access/actions.
Verify trusted runtime policy blocks it while intended actions succeed; record tested attack scope.
severity: High to Critical when untrusted text can trigger privileged actions or data exfiltration; model compliance alone is insufficient evidence.
automation_limits: Prompt wording or injection tests cannot prove complete resistance. Tool permissions, data boundaries, human approvals, and changing model behavior need separate validation.
